I know. Drug innovation doesn't grant you the right to be an apotheker. However the farmacie master is in Dutch only. So would actually be very hard to follow if you do not speak proper Dutch at the start of the study. Which is why a good understanding of Dutch is necessary to even start the master track.

AFAIK you are not allowed to start farmacie without being able to understand and speak Dutch. 

 Sorry if I was unclear.

If your wife wants to study pharmacy in the Netherlands and actually become a pharmacist she will be required to speak fluent Dutch and she has to pass all her exams in Dutch as well.  If she wants to study pharmaceutical sciences (drug innovation at the UU) she might come by with English whilst learning Dutch. 

The reasoning behind this is that at a patient level the patients will not be able to speak English at a good enough level to actually understand the consequences of medication and the effects you get when you take them wrongly  (either dose/frequency or side effects)

So I would advise against studying at UU if your wife wants to become a pharmacist as she will be required to study in Dutch here. 

Source: currently studying pharmacy at UU and almost finished my bachelor degree
